entries.title: Jeremiah 22:1
segments: According to some, the prophet addressed the words of this chapter to Zedekiah, and embodied in them his former predictions concerning Shallum, Jehoiakim, and Coniah.  Thus the denunciation in hte last verse would refer to Zedekiah.  But we may better refer the prophecy, at least as far as verse 19, to the reign of Jehoiakim; what follows concerning Coniah being either spoken in anticipation of his disastrous reign, or written during it at a later date.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:6
segments:
Gilead--the head of Lebanon; Gilead was the mountainous region on the east of Jordan, south of the river Jabbok.  Like Lebanon it was celebrated for its majesty and beauty.  The meaning is, that however precious to God is the royal house of David, with the kingdom intrusted to it, God will make both utterly desolate for their sins. 
 
No outward nearness or sacredness of relation to God will screen men from his wrath when they persist in trampling under foot his laws.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:8
segments:
vv 8-9. 
 
As God has distinguished his covenant people above all nations of the earth by his wonderful interpositions in their behalf, so will he make their punishment in like manner conspicuous when they sin against him, that the inhabitants of the world may see it and fear before him.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:10
segments:
For the dead; the reference seems to be to Josiah. 
 
  Him that goeth away; that is, Shallum.

The dead are beyond the reach of our prayers and sympathies, and immoderate grief for them is forbidden by the spirit of true religion; the living who are in distress may rather claim our tears and supplications in their behalf.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:11
segments: Shallum; generally supposed to have been the same as Jehoahaz, whom Pharaoh-Necho carried captive into Egypt, after a reign of three months.
He was a younger brother, but "the people of the land" preferred him before Jehoiakim.  His name was probably changed upon his accession to the throne, as was that of Jehoiakim,
; and Zedekiah,

. 
 
God will not spare wicked children for the piety of their fathers.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:13
segments: That buildeth his house by unrighteousness; the reference is to Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah and successor of Jehoahaz.  That the reigning monarch is addressed is plain, from

.  He was an avaricious, luxurious, and unrighteous king, who oppressed and plundered the people for his own aggrandizement. 
 
vv 13-19. 
 
Rulers who rob and oppress the people for their own aggrandizement, are alike odious to God and man, and they generally come to an ignominious end, with none to mourn for them or honor them in death.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:18
segments:
For him; that is, for him and the members of his family, as the words, "Ah, sister," show. 
 
  Ah, sister; this probably refers to his queen, who was afterwards carried captive to Babylon with Jehoiachin her son.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:19
segments: Buried with the burial of an ass; that is, shall be left unburied.
Drawn and cast forth; that is, which is drawn and cast forth, the words referring to the body of the ass, not to Jehoiakim, who probably died in Babylon.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:20
segments:
Go up to Lebanon--in Bashon; the address is to "the daughter of Zion."  Let her cry from the mountain-tops, that all may hear her wailings. 
 
  From the passages; either, from the passages that lead out of the land to Babylon; or better, "from Abarim," a mountainous ridge east of the lower Jordan and the Dead sea.
Thy lovers; the foreign nations to whom thou trustedst for help.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:22
segments: The alliances of God's ancient people with their heathen neighbors ended in disappointment and ruin; so will it ever be with those who forsake the living God for earthly confidences.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:23
segments:
Inhabitant of Lebanon--makest thy nest in the cedars; a double reference to the beauty of mount Zion, which rivalled that of Lebanon; and to the palaces built with cedar-wood from Lebanon, that adorned its heights. 
 
  How gracious; rather, "how much to be commiserated."

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:24
segments: Coniah; elsewhere called Jeconiah,
; and Jehoiachin,

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:28
segments:
Idol; rather, "earthen vessel."  The question of the prophet expresses astonishment at his fate. 
 
  Wherefore are they cast out; the prophet leaves the people to infer the answer.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:29
segments: O earth, earth, earth; he solemnly calls upon the earth to witness his prediction.  Compare De 32.1; Isa 1.2.

entries.title: Jeremiah 22:30
segments:
This man; Coniah. 
 
  Childless; not in the absolute sense, for he had children,
, one of whom is named in our Lord's genealogy,

, and this is implied in the words following: "No man of his seed shall prosper."  But he was childless in the sense immediately explained, that none of his seed should occupy the throne of David in Jerusalem.  Zedekiah, who reigned after him, was his brother.  The prophet her refers to the earthly throne of David. 
 
The earthly kingdom of David began with righteous rulers, and gained strength and glory by obedience to God's laws; it was destroyed by wicked and corrupt rulers, leading a wicked and corrupt people in iniquity and rebellion against God.  Herein is it set forth as an example to all nations.
